survey: A square, rounded portable music player floats in the frame with earbuds attached. The front face points almost straight at the viewer, turned slightly so that its left edge runs at about 64° and its top and bottom edges at about 164°. Its thickness shows only along the right and bottom sides, so the camera is slightly above and to the left. All the body's edges agree on that one view. The big round play button sits on the front face. It fits an ellipse with width ratio 0.88, squashed by about the same amount as the small round button below it (0.95), with short axes of 125° and 131°, which suits a face turned only a little. The red, orange and green indicator dots sit in a row that slopes like the face's top and bottom edges. The play button and the small button line up along the face's left-edge direction, so repeated elements follow the surface. A cable plug comes straight out of the top face. The cable loops to the right, passes behind the body and splits into two earbuds at the bottom. The earbud openings are ellipses with ratios 0.36 and 0.48 and nearly horizontal short axes, so both point roughly left toward the viewer. They are consistent with each other and with the stems that rise toward the cable. There is no ground plane, so there is no contact angle to check.
